submitted.rationale: Index 5 (Mn 0.23, Sb 0.77) had the highest photocurrent of the three measurements, 3.1e-7 A. Photocurrent rose as Mn fell: -2e-8 A at Mn 0.50, 1.4e-7 A at Mn 0.31 and 3.1e-7 A at Mn 0.23. MEGNet predicts gaps below the photon energy for the Sb-rich phases, e.g. about 2.19 eV for MnSb4O12, which fits this trend.

rejected.reason: Measured -2e-8 A, so the Mn-rich MnSbO4 region has essentially no photoactivity
Might be better, but untested because the merit budget ran out

consultations.verdict: Weak support. MACE puts the Mn-Sb-O phase at Mn:Sb 1:2 on the hull (Ehull 0), so compositions near Mn 0.33 should form a well-defined ternary (trirutile/rutile-type) oxide. The MEGNet HSE gap of 0.016 eV for MnSb2O6 is almost certainly a DFT artefact and doesn't inform the choice. Index 3 (Mn 0.31) is close to that stoichiometry, which makes it a reasonable first probe.

Support. MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of about 1.84 eV for MnSbO4 (Mn:Sb 1:1). That is below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so the phase should absorb visible light. Index 11 (Mn 0.50) sits at this stoichiometry and tests the Mn-rich side of the line.

Support. MEGNet predicts an HSE gap of about 2.19 eV for MnSb4O12 (Mn 0.2), so a Sb-rich phase should absorb below 3.22 eV. The measurements also point this way: index 3 (Mn 0.31) was positive and index 11 (Mn 0.50) was about zero. Index 5 (Mn 0.23) tests the Sb-rich side between these.
